rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a very poor-quality early blastocyst with poorly defined/degenerative ICM and TE and overall disorganized appearance. Minor issue: uses '0' as early blastocyst expansion and mentions debris/fragments somewhat speculatively from the image.

Integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, sperm parameters, endometrium, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo prognosis well. Slightly limited by nonspecific handling of the diagnosis and some generic comments on paternal age/oocyte quality.

Reasoning is logical and consistent: severe morphologic compromise drives the poor prognosis despite favorable uterine and reserve factors. Minor overstatement in declaring the embryo essentially non-viable from morphology alone.

Generally consistent with Gardner-based interpretation and poor prognosis for DD embryos, but recommending to categorically avoid transfer and calling it non-viable is stronger than guideline-based morphology alone supports. Freeze-all suggestion is also not well justified for this exact scenario.

Provides clear next steps including counseling, review of other embryos, lab review, and future-cycle considerations such as PGT-A discussion. Some recommendations are useful but a few are generic or not tightly tailored to this specific case.
